Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Investments Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the operator instructions are to press star one to ask a question. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Investments' Second Quarter 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; David Wong, Head of Distribution; Emily Carter, Head of Operations; and Robert Kline, Head of Risk Management.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust management fee revenue growth and sustained AUM expansion. Our AUM grew to a record $1.45 trillion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, John. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Investments delivered strong results in Q2. Our revenue was $2.82 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM from net inflows and market appreciation, alongside resilient average fee rates. Our expenses were $1.95 billion, resulting in net income of $850 million. Our expense ratio improved due to operational efficiencies and disciplined cost management.

Let me now turn to our core revenue drivers: management fee revenue and the trends in our average fee rate. As you know, management fees remain the bedrock of our recurring revenue stream at Apex Global Investments, representing approximately 85% of our total fee revenue in Q2. They are calculated as a percentage of our average daily AUM and are highly predictable given our long-duration client relationships and institutional mandate mix.

For the second quarter, management fee revenue came in at $2.82 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY growth, driven by a combination of robust net inflows, favorable market tailwinds, and disciplined mix management. On a full-year basis through June 30th, management fees totaled $10.9 billion, positioning us well for our FY24 guidance midpoint of $11.5 to $12.0 billion.

Our ending AUM reached a record $1.45 trillion, up 9% from Q1 and 22% YoY, reflecting $28 billion in long-term net inflows—the strongest Q2 since 2021—plus $85 billion in market appreciation. Average AUM for the quarter, the key denominator for fee revenue, was $1.38 trillion, benefiting from the S&P 500's 15% YTD rally and solid performance across our diversified mandates.

Drilling into the average fee rate, which ticked down 2 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 45.8 bps, and 4 bps YoY from 46.2 bps. This reflects ongoing industry-wide fee compression, but we've meaningfully outperformed our peers by stabilizing rates above the 40 bps threshold that Vanguard and State Street have pulled many clients toward. For context, the broader industry average, per Morningstar data, sits at around 42 bps for active managers, with passive ETFs averaging sub-10 bps. Our resilience here stems from our product mix: high-margin alternatives and active equities still comprise 55% of AUM, versus the street's 45% tilt toward index strategies.

Breaking it down by asset class: Equities, at 52% of AUM or $752 billion, fees here averaged 52 bps, flat QoQ. We saw $15 billion in net inflows, led by our large-cap growth strategies like the Apex Global Equity Partners fund, which returned 18% YTD net of fees, outpacing the MSCI World Index by 450 bps. However, fee pressure persists from ETF competition—our own Apex S&P 500 ETF, with a 7 bps expense ratio, captured $8 billion in flows but diluted the segment rate by 1 bp. We're countering this with smart beta overlays, adding 5-10 bps of alpha-seeking tilts without fully sacrificing scale.

Fixed Income, 25% of AUM at $362 billion: Average fee of 38 bps, down 3 bps YoY amid yield curve normalization. Inflows of $6 billion were anchored by our short-duration and ESG bond ladders, which benefited from the Bloomberg Aggregate's 2.5% Q2 return. We've implemented selective fee waivers on $50 billion of core bond AUM to defend against PIMCO and BlackRock's ultra-competitive 25-30 bps offerings, but this shaved just 0.5 bps off the blended rate.

Alternatives/Multi-Asset, 18% of AUM at $261 billion: Our crown jewel, with fees at a robust 72 bps, up 1 bp QoQ on higher allocations to private credit and infrastructure. Net inflows hit $7 billion, fueled by institutional demand for our Apex Private Markets platform, which now manages $120 billion including $40 billion in evergreen structures. Yields here remain attractive—think 9-12% targeted IRRs—allowing us to resist fee cuts even as peers like KKR and Apollo face LP pushback.

ETFs and Model Portfolios, 5% of AUM at $72 billion: Fastest-growing at 25% YoY, with fees at 12 bps. This segment added $4 billion in retail flows via our Apex Core ETF suite, leveraging white-label partnerships with Schwab and Fidelity platforms.

Geographically, our fee trends vary meaningfully: North America, 65% of AUM, fees at 48 bps, stable. U.S. institutional flows were stellar at $18 billion, but wirehouse channels saw mild compression from Merrill Lynch's push into SMAs—separately managed accounts—which now represent 20% of our U.S. retail AUM at blended 35 bps.

Europe, 20% of AUM: 44 bps average, down 2 bps on MiFID II cost disclosure pressures. Strong $5 billion inflows into UCITS ETFs, but active equity mandates faced headwinds from DWS and Amundi's low-cost alternatives. Our London-based sustainable strategies mitigated this, adding 50 bps of fee premium.

Asia-Pacific, 10% of AUM: 50 bps, our highest, but growth slowed to $2 billion inflows amid China's property woes. We're pivoting to Japan and India, where our active small-cap funds command 60+ bps, outshining local players like Nomura.

Rest of World, 5%: Latin America and Middle East sovereign wealth mandates held firm at 65 bps, with $1 billion inflows tied to inflation-linked real assets.

We've been proactive on the tech front to stem compression. Our proprietary FeeForge platform—built on a customized Aladdin-like stack—has enabled dynamic pricing for 30% of AUM, using AI-driven client segmentation to upsell performance-based tiers. This added 1.5 bps to Q2 revenue versus static models. Additionally, we've scaled direct indexing for HNW clients, launching 50 personalized strategies post-tax lot optimization, which carry 40-55 bps versus generic ETFs.

On the institutional side, our RFP win rate hit 65%, up from 55% last year, thanks to bundled services like ESG analytics and derivatives overlays, preserving 5-10 bps premiums. We've also de-risked $100 billion of legacy high-fee mandates by migrating to active ETFs, blending alpha with ETF liquidity at 25 bps—capturing flows without full capitulation.

Looking ahead, we expect continued fee headwinds from passive proliferation—BlackRock's iShares now at $3.5 trillion—but our mix shift targets mid-40s bps long-term, supported by alternatives growing to 25% of AUM by FY26. Net inflows guidance remains $100-120 billion for the year, with equities and alts leading. Key strategies include scaling in ETFs targeting $200 billion in ETF AUM by 2026 via zero-commission integrations on Robinhood and Vanguard's ecosystem; alternatives expansion with $50 billion in new private credit commitments, leveraging our GP stakes for 100 bps+ economics; tech-enabled SMAs rolling out to 40% of retail AUM, countering fee drag with personalization; and ESG premiums, 15% fee uplift on $150 billion AUM, aligned with EU SFDR and SEC climate rules.

In summary, while average fee rates face structural pressure, our revenue growth outpaces AUM expansion by 300 bps, underscoring mix discipline and client stickiness—our average mandate tenure is 12 years. This positions us to deliver 10-12% annual fee revenue CAGR through the decade, even in a low-fee world.

Good afternoon, everyone. As of September 30th, 2024, our total AUM stood at $1.45 trillion, marking a robust 18.2% year-over-year increase from $1.226 trillion at the end of Q3 2023. Quarter-over-quarter, we grew 5.1% from $1.379 trillion at the end of Q2. This performance significantly outpaced the industry average, where peers like BlackRock and State Street reported YoY AUM growth in the mid-teens, per Morningstar data.

Breaking down the drivers, net inflows contributed $28 billion over the past 12 months, with $7.2 billion in Q3 alone—our strongest quarterly inflow since Q4 2021. Market appreciation added $156 billion YoY, fueled by broad equity rallies and a rebound in alternatives, while FX translation and other factors were a modest tailwind of about $12 billion, primarily from our Eurozone exposures strengthening against the USD. On a QoQ basis, market returns drove $62 billion of growth, with inflows adding $8 billion net of outflows.

Our AUM composition at quarter-end: Equities at $652 billion, 45% of total, +22.4% YoY, +7.2% QoQ. Fixed Income $435 billion, 30%, +12.8% YoY, +3.1% QoQ. Alternatives $290 billion, 20%, +25.6% YoY, +6.8% QoQ. Multi-Asset & Cash Equivalents $73 billion, 5%, +8.5% YoY, +1.2% QoQ.

Equities delivered the star performance with 22.4% YoY growth, propelled by the S&P 500's 28% total return over the past year, driven by the AI megatrend—think NVIDIA's 150%+ surge and the Magnificent Seven's dominance. Our active equity strategies, including the Apex Global Equity Fund up 32% annualized, saw $12 billion in net inflows, while our suite of 15 ETFs, like the APEX AI Innovators ETF with $18B AUM tracking a custom AI index, benefited from $4.5 billion in organic flows. QoQ, we captured 7.2% growth, outpacing the MSCI World Index by 200 bps, thanks to tactical overweight in US large-cap growth and selective EM exposure via our Asia ex-Japan fund.

Fixed Income AUM reached $435 billion, up 12.8% YoY but more muted QoQ at 3.1%, reflecting the Bloomberg Global Aggregate's modest 5% return amid the Fed's September 50 bps rate cut. Duration positioning paid off—our intermediate core-plus strategies averaged 4.2 years duration, generating 150 bps of excess return versus benchmarks. Institutional mandates, particularly from pension funds, drove $5 billion in inflows, with standout products like the Apex Sustainable Credit Fund $22B AUM attracting ESG-focused allocators. We're cautiously optimistic on spreads tightening further into 2025, with planned launches of two CLO ETFs targeting 8-10% yields.

Alternatives continues to be our fastest-growing segment at $290 billion, surging 25.6% YoY and 6.8% QoQ. Private markets led with $45 billion in evergreen funds, including our Apex Private Equity Partners VI vintage 2023, $15B closed at hard cap, which deployed into secondaries amid dry powder fatigue industry-wide. Hedge fund strategies $120B AUM returned 9.2% net YTD, beating the HFRI Fund Weighted Composite by 300 bps via macro and event-driven tilts. Real assets, at 15% of alts, grew on infrastructure tailwinds—our Global Renewables Infrastructure Fund $28B capitalized on IRA-driven US projects and EU Green Deal subsidies. Inflows here totaled $6.8 billion in Q3, skewed toward high-net-worth and family office channels seeking 12-15% IRRs in a higher-for-longer rate environment.

Regionally, North America remains dominant at 58% of AUM $841B, with 20% YoY growth from retail and 401(k) platforms like our partnership with Fidelity. EMEA 28%, $406B expanded 16% YoY, bolstered by £3 billion inflows into UCITS ETFs post-UK pension reforms. Asia-Pacific 14%, $203B accelerated to 22% YoY growth, driven by mandates from sovereign wealth funds like GIC and Temasek into our China+1 strategies, navigating US-China tensions via Vietnam and India exposures.

Strategically, we're leveraging technology to sustain this momentum. Our proprietary Apex Alpha platform—powered by machine learning for alpha generation and client personalization—now covers 70% of AUM, enabling 25% faster rebalancing and contributing to 50 bps of fee compression benefits passed to clients. We've also accelerated our ETF pipeline, launching four new products in Q3 totaling $2.5B seed capital, targeting thematic areas like quantum computing and decarbonization. M&A remains opportunistic; post our Q1 acquisition of a $35B European alternatives boutique, integration is yielding 15% cost synergies.

Looking forward, we guide to $1.55-$1.60 trillion AUM by year-end, assuming MSCI World +4-6% Q4 and continued 8-10% annualized inflows. Risks include geopolitical flare-ups in the Middle East impacting EM fixed income, but our 45/30/20 diversification and active risk management—targeting 10-12% volatility—position us resiliently.

Good afternoon, everyone. Our total net flows for the period came in at $14.2 billion – a robust performance that exceeded our internal guidance by 15% and marked our strongest quarter since Q4 2021. This represents inflows of $28.7 billion against outflows of $14.5 billion, delivering a net flow margin of 49.5%, up 320 basis points sequentially from Q2's $9.8 billion.

To contextualize, our total AUM stood at $1.47 trillion at quarter-end, reflecting 4.2% organic growth from net flows alone, before market appreciation added another 2.8%. Year-over-year, Q3 net flows surged 28% from $11.1 billion, underscoring the resilience of our franchise amid a volatile macro environment characterized by the Fed's 25bps hike in July, persistent inflation at 3.7% CPI, and the S&P 500's 1.7% dip driven by tech sector rotation.

By product type, where we saw pronounced strength in passive and alternatives strategies: ETFs, which now comprise 42% of our AUM, drove $9.6 billion in net inflows – 68% of the total. Our flagship Apex Core Equity ETF suite, tracking the MSCI World Index with a low 0.08% TER, attracted $6.2 billion, fueled by retail rebalancing into large-cap growth amid AI hype around names like Nvidia and Microsoft. We also launched the Apex ESG Global Leaders ETF in late Q2, which garnered $2.1 billion in its first full quarter, tapping into the $40 trillion global sustainable investing wave per Morningstar data. This outperforms peers like Vanguard's ESG funds, which saw flat flows amid greenwashing scrutiny.

Fixed Income contributed $3.4 billion, reversing Q2's mild outflow. With yields on 10-year Treasuries climbing to 4.3%, investors rotated into our active short-duration strategies, including the Apex Ultra-Short Credit Fund yielding 5.2% annualized, pulling in $2.8 billion from institutional defined benefit plans. Outflows here were minimal at $0.9 billion, primarily tactical redemptions from legacy high-yield mandates.

Equities Active posted $1.8 billion net, a sequential improvement from $0.7 billion, as our quant-driven long-only strategies benefited from small-cap outperformance. The Apex AlphaSeek U.S. Mid-Cap Fund, leveraging machine learning models trained on 20+ years of factor data, saw $1.2 billion in HNW inflows via our robo-advisor platform.

Alternatives and Multi-Asset rounded out with $2.9 billion, led by private credit and infrastructure. Our Apex Direct Lending Partnership, seeded with $500 million from a sovereign wealth fund, closed on $1.7 billion commitments, capitalizing on the illiquidity premium in a 7%+ SOFR environment. This segment's 12-month flow yield now stands at 2.1%, rivaling Blackstone's private credit arm.

Client type segmentation: Retail and wealth management channels, representing 55% of flows, delivered $8.9 billion net – up 35% YoY – propelled by our Apex WealthConnect app, which onboarded 250,000 new users via embedded finance integrations with platforms like Wealthfront and Robinhood. Institutional flows hit $5.3 billion, with strong uptake from European pension funds reallocating from cash equivalents post-ECB rate pauses.

Regional commentary: North America 65% of AUM: $9.8 billion net, or 69% of total. U.S. wirehouses like Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley funneled $4.5 billion into our beta-plus ETFs, while Canadian flows accelerated on commodity tilts amid oil's rebound to $85/barrel.

EMEA 22% of AUM: Steady at $2.7 billion, despite outflows from UK DB schemes amid gilt volatility. Our Dublin-domiciled UCITS ETFs captured $1.4 billion from Continental platforms like Allianz GI, bolstered by MiFID II-compliant ESG disclosures.

Asia-Pacific 13% of AUM: The standout at $3.4 billion – double Q2 – driven by $2.1 billion from Japanese GPIFs rotating into our yen-hedged equity ETFs following the BOJ's yield curve tweak. Chinese HNWIs via Hong Kong contributed $0.8 billion to alternatives, navigating regulatory headwinds through our QDLP-qualified feeder funds.

Sequentially, flows accelerated 45% from Q2, reversing the summer lull as 60/40 portfolios rebalanced post the great cash exodus – U.S. money market funds saw $120 billion outflows per ICI data, much of which rotated to us. YoY, we're up 28%, outpacing the industry's 12% per eVestment, thanks to our 15% AUM share in smart-beta ETFs.

Key headwinds included $3.2 billion in outflows from underperforming emerging market equities, hit by China's property woes, and $1.8 billion from active small-cap mandates lagging the Russell 2000's flat performance. However, our flow retention ratio improved to 92% from 88% YoY, reflecting sticky institutional relationships.

We've invested heavily in tech to sustain this momentum. Our proprietary FlowOptics platform, powered by Snowflake data warehousing and Palantir's AIP for predictive analytics, flagged high-propensity inflow segments 14 days early, enabling targeted campaigns that boosted conversion rates by 22%. Additionally, our API integrations with advisor tech stacks like Envestnet's Tamarac captured 30% more RIA flows. Looking ahead, we're rolling out blockchain-based tokenization for private assets in Q4, partnering with Securitize to unlock $50 billion in illiquid AUM for retail access – a play mirroring Hamilton Lane's model.

These flows validate our Active Passive Hybrid strategy, blending low-cost indexing with alpha overlays, which now accounts for 28% of AUM and delivers 150bps excess return over benchmarks net of fees. We're prioritizing duration-neutral fixed income and AI-themed equities, positioning for a soft landing scenario with 4.5% GDP growth.

For Q4, we guide to $12-16 billion net flows, assuming stable markets, with upside from our $10 billion private markets pipeline and new launches like the Apex Carbon Credit ETF. Risks include prolonged high rates pressuring equities or geopolitical flares in the Middle East impacting EM.

Overall, this quarter reaffirms Apex's leadership in a consolidating industry – with BlackRock and Vanguard dominating scale, our nimble 1.5% market share punches above its weight through innovation.

Before diving into forward guidance, I'd like to provide a detailed walkthrough of how changes in our AUM directly drove our top-line performance this quarter. In asset management, revenue is fundamentally tied to AUM through our fee-based model, where base management fees, calculated as a percentage of average daily AUM, represent approximately 85% of our total revenue. We also generate performance fees on certain alternative strategies and institutional mandates, which can amplify earnings in favorable markets.

Our ending AUM reached a record $1.25 trillion as of June 30, 2024, up 12% year-over-year and 4% quarter-over-quarter. Average AUM for the quarter was $1.18 trillion, a 14% increase from Q2 2023. This translated to $2.65 billion in total revenue, beating our consensus estimate of $2.55 billion and up 15% YoY. Our blended fee rate held steady at 44.5 basis points—down just 10 bps YoY due to some product mix shift toward lower-fee ETFs, but more than offset by higher performance fees of $185 million, up 25% YoY from strong alpha generation in our private credit and hedge fund strategies.

To unpack the AUM drivers: Market appreciation contributed +9% to ending AUM growth, or roughly $105 billion. This was led by a broad equity rally, with the S&P 500 up 15% YTD and the MSCI World Index gaining 12%. Our equity AUM, 55% of total at $687 billion, benefited disproportionately, growing 18% YoY. Key performers included our suite of ETFs tracking the Nasdaq-100 and Russell 2000, where tech-heavy exposure to the AI boom drove outsized gains. Fixed income AUM, 25% or $312 billion, saw more modest +2% market-driven growth amid Fed rate cut expectations.

Organic net flows added +5%, or $58 billion, marking our 11th straight quarter of positive inflows. Long-term net inflows hit $45 billion, with ETFs capturing $32 billion—fueled by our launch of three new active ETFs in Q1, including a thematic AI & Robotics ETF that's already amassed $4.2 billion in AUM. Institutional separate accounts added $12 billion, particularly from sovereign wealth funds rotating into our multi-asset credit platform amid high-yield opportunities in leveraged loans yielding 8-10%. Offsetting this modestly were $13 billion in outflows from legacy active equity mutual funds, reflecting ongoing secular pressure—down 20% YoY but still a headwind we view as largely priced in.

FX was a -2% drag, or -$22 billion, primarily from a stronger USD against the euro and yen, impacting our EMEA and APAC books, where 35% of AUM is non-USD denominated.

Regionally: Americas 65% of AUM $812 billion: +16% YoY growth, driven by retail flows into low-cost beta products. EMEA 25% $312 billion: +8% growth despite outflows from UK defined-contribution pensions. APAC 10% $125 billion: Flat QoQ but +5% YoY.

These AUM dynamics underscore three key initiatives: Scale through ETFs and indexing, with ETFs now 40% of AUM, margins expanded 150 bps to 42%; diversification into alternatives now 15% at $187 billion; and tech-enabled client retention with AI-driven flow forecasting improving net flow retention by 5% QoQ.

Looking ahead, we expect Q3 average AUM of $1.22-$1.25 trillion, assuming flat markets and continued $10-15 billion monthly net flows. Revenue sensitivity: every $10 billion AUM swing impacts quarterly revenue by ~$45 million at current fee rates.

I'll now turn to our outlook for the full year 2024 and into early 2025, providing guidance on revenue and expenses. Our guidance assumes no material market disruptions, a continuation of the current macroeconomic environment with U.S. 10-year Treasury yields stabilizing around 4.0-4.25%, and global equity markets trading at forward P/E multiples in line with historical averages—S&P 500 at 20-21x and MSCI World ex-U.S. at 14-15x. We're also factoring in ongoing fee compression in core beta strategies, offset by growth in higher-margin alternatives and active equities.

We expect full-year 2024 consolidated revenues to come in between $4.85 billion and $5.05 billion, representing 9-13% growth over 2023's $4.45 billion. This reflects organic AUM expansion, favorable market beta, and selective performance fee realization.

AUM trajectory: Year-end 2024 AUM of $825-850 billion, up from $785 billion as of Q3. Implies 5-8% organic growth from net flows totaling $45-55 billion, with long-term net inflows accelerating to $15-20 billion in Q4. Institutional $30-35 billion; retail $15-20 billion via VertexCore digital platform managing over $120 billion in RIA-sourced assets.

Management fees 85% of revenues, grow 8-11% to $4.15-4.30 billion. Average fee rates 52-53 bps from 54 bps in 2023. iApex ETFs captured $18 billion inflows YTD at 18 bps; private markets 85-110 bps. Performance fees $250-300 million, up 20-40%, from Apex Opportunities Fund III pacing toward 22% net IRR.

Regionally, U.S. 10-12% growth; Europe 6-8%; APAC 15-18%. Launching three new active ETFs in Q1 2025 on AI infrastructure and clean energy; scaling Apex Alpha hedge fund-of-funds.

Expenses: Full-year adjusted operating expenses $3.25-3.40 billion, up 7-10%, implying 33-34% margins—expanding 100-150 bps.

Compensation $1.80-1.90 billion; G&A $850-900 million; Technology and distribution $600-650 million, including VertexOS and robo-advisory. Q4 sequential growth 1-2%. Goal 32-35% margins by 2026.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by maintaining diversified allocations across asset classes and leveraging our proprietary alpha generation platforms. We launched the Apex AI Innovators ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $4.5 billion in inflows and strong tracking performance against our custom AI index.

David Wong: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in North America and EMEA are paying off, as evidenced by deepened integrations with RIAs and retirement platforms.

Turning now to our distribution partnerships and channel expansion efforts, which continue to be a cornerstone of our organic growth strategy here at Apex Global Investments. We've been laser-focused on diversifying our distribution beyond traditional wirehouses and broker-dealers into high-growth channels like RIAs, model marketplaces, retirement platforms, and international wealth managers. In Q3, distribution partnerships accounted for 28% of our total net inflows of $14.2 billion, up from 22% in the prior quarter. This includes $4.1 billion in organic flows from new and expanded RIA relationships alone. Overall, AUM from partnership-sourced assets grew 17% quarter-over-quarter to $285 billion, representing 42% of our total $675 billion AUM.

RIA expansion has been transformative. We've deepened integrations with Envestnet's Tamarac and Orion Advisor Tech, where our UMA models now represent 15% of their top-decile strategies. Expanded agreement with Creative Planning rolled out direct indexing across their $150 billion platform, generating $900 million YTD with 25% higher retention.

On retirement, collaboration with Vestwell and Empower embedded our target-date funds into over 500 new 401(k) plans, capturing $2.3 billion. In EMEA, partnership with UBS distributed active fixed-income to 120 branches, adding €3.2 billion. In APAC, JV with DBS Private Bank launched white-labeled Asia ex-Japan equity ETF, pulling in SGD 1.2 billion.

Our API-first ApexConnect 2.0 supports real-time analytics and blockchain NAV reconciliation, boosting partner NPS to 78. Pipeline: 15 new RIA deals for $10-12 billion H2 inflows.

Emily Carter: Thank you, David. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure, including platforms like FeeForge, FlowOptics, and Apex Alpha, which have resulted in increased efficiency, reduced operational risk, and faster rebalancing across 70% of AUM. We are also focused on scaling cloud-native tech stacks and API integrations to support distribution growth and client personalization.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Emily. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and geopolitical risks, including those in EM fixed income and China property, and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes stress testing for 20% AUM drawdowns, dynamic pricing models, and diversification targets of 45/30/20 across asset classes to cap volatility at 10-12%.

John Reynolds: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes our disciplined capital allocation strategy, which remains the cornerstone of delivering superior total shareholder returns.

As we close out the first half with record AUM of $785 billion—up 14% YoY and 8% QoQ—our framework prioritizes organic reinvestment, selective M&A, shareholder returns, and prudent debt management. Hierarchy: Organic reinvestment $450 million to tech like Pinnacle Alpha reducing drift 25%; seeding $100 million into private credit and ESG ETFs.

M&A: $1.2 billion Horizon Alternatives acquisition boosting alts to $120 billion, 50 bps fee lift. Shareholder returns: Dividend up 12% to $0.42/share; $850 million buybacks. Balance sheet fortress: A- rating, refinanced debt at 4.1%.

Forward: $600 million deploy, 40% tech/AI, 30% seeding, 30% M&A; APAC 30% net new money. Positions for 12-15% EPS growth.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Morningstar.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more details on management fee revenue trends and fee rate pressures?

John Reynolds: Good morning, Alex. Michael, would you take that?

Michael Chen: Absolutely. As I detailed earlier, management fees hit $2.82 billion, up 12% YoY, with average fee rate at 45.8 bps despite industry compression. Our mix—55% high-margin alts and equities—has stabilized us above peers, and tech like FeeForge adds dynamic pricing uplift. We're targeting mid-40s long-term via alternatives growth.

Alex Rivera: Thank you. And a follow-up on revenue guidance incorporating AUM impacts?

Michael Chen: Our FY24 revenue guide is $4.85-5.05 billion, driven by $825-850B year-end AUM. Every $10B AUM change impacts revenue by ~$45M quarterly. Flows and markets remain key, with performance fees upside from 22% IRR funds.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jamie Lee with Goldman Sachs.

Jamie Lee: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Apex Global Equity Partners fund?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Jamie. The fund returned 18% YTD net, outpacing MSCI World by 450 bps, thanks to large-cap growth overweight and AI tilts. Inflows of $15B reflect strong institutional demand, with smart beta overlays preserving alpha.

Jamie Lee: And how is the new product Apex AI Innovators ETF performing relative to expectations?

David Wong: Early reception exceeds expectations with $4.5B inflows. Thematic AI focus via custom index has captured retail and RIA flows, leveraging partnerships with Schwab for distribution. On track for $10B+ by year-end.

Operator: Our next question comes from Taylor Kim with Barclays.

Taylor Kim: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Emily Carter: Certainly. Investments in Apex Alpha and FlowOptics have cut rebalancing times 25%, onboarding 40%, and boosted conversion 22%. Cloud migrations reduced IT costs 12%, supporting 70% AUM coverage and scalability for tokenized assets.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Patel with JPMorgan.

Chris Patel: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Robert Kline: Thanks, Chris. MiFID II, SFDR, and SEC rules are monitored closely via enhanced ESG reporting and compliance tech. We've de-risked legacy mandates to active ETFs, stress-tested for volatility/geopolitics, maintaining 1.5x coverage and 92% flow retention. Diversification keeps us resilient.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to John Reynolds for closing remarks.

John Reynolds: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Investments. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Management fee revenue and average fee r: Management fee revenue reached $2.82B in Q2, up 12% YoY and 5% QoQ, marking 11th straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth; full-year through June $10.9B, guiding to $11.5-12.0B midpoint. Average fee rate 45.8 bps, down 2 bps QoQ and 4 bps YoY from 46.2 bps due to industry compression, but resilient above peers via high-margin alternatives/equities (55% AUM), dynamic pricing tech like FeeForge adding 1.5 bps, targeting mid-40s bps long-term with alts growth.
aspect_summary.AUM growth (YoY, QoQ) and breakdown by a: Ending AUM hit record $1.45T in Q2 (up 22% YoY, 9% QoQ), average AUM $1.38T; as of Sep 30 $1.45T (18.2% YoY, 5.1% QoQ). Breakdown: Equities 45-52% ($652-752B, +22.4% YoY, +7.2% QoQ); Fixed Income 25-30% ($362-435B, +12.8% YoY, +3.1% QoQ); Alternatives 18-20% ($261-290B, +25.6% YoY, +6.8% QoQ); ETFs/Model 5% ($72B). Growth from $28B Q2 net inflows, market appreciation.
aspect_summary.Total net flows (inflows/outflows) for t: Q2 long-term net inflows $28B (strongest since 2021); Q3 $14.2B net ($28.7B inflows vs $14.5B outflows, up 45% QoQ, 28% YoY), exceeding guidance; ETFs $9.6B, FI $3.4B, Active Equities $1.8B, Alts/Multi $2.9B. Year-to-date strong, guiding $100-120B FY, Q4 $12-16B.
aspect_summary.Revenue and expense guidance: FY24 revenue $4.85-5.05B (9-13% growth); management fees $4.15-4.30B (8-11% growth, 52-53 bps rates); performance fees $250-300M (20-40% up); year-end AUM $825-850B or $1.55-1.60T, Q3 avg $1.22-1.25T. Expenses $3.25-3.40B (7-10% up), 33-34% margins (expanding 100-150 bps), compensation $1.80-1.90B, G&A $850-900M, tech/distribution $600-650M.
aspect_summary.Distribution partnerships and channel ex: Partnerships drove 28% of Q3 net inflows ($4.1B from RIAs); partnership AUM $285B (42% total). Key: RIA integrations (Envestnet Tamarac/Orion, Creative Planning direct indexing $900M YTD); retirement (Vestwell/Empower $2.3B, 500+ 401(k) plans); EMEA (UBS €3.2B); APAC (DBS JV SGD 1.2B). ApexConnect 2.0 APIs boost NPS to 78; 15 new RIA deals for $10-12B H2 inflows.
aspect_summary.Impact of AUM changes on revenue: Revenue ($2.82B Q2, 12% YoY up) driven by higher average AUM ($1.38T Q2, up from markets/inflows) at resilient 45.8 bps; management fees 85% of revenue. Every $10B AUM swing impacts quarterly revenue ~$45M; FY24 guide reflects AUM expansion/market beta, offset by fee compression via ETF mix shift, boosted by performance fees $185M (+25% YoY).
aspect_summary.Capital allocation strategy: Disciplined framework: organic reinvestment $450M (tech like Pinnacle Alpha); seeding $100M (private credit/ESG ETFs); M&A $1.2B (Horizon Alternatives, +50 bps fees, alts to $120B); shareholder returns (dividend +12% to $0.42/share, $850M buybacks). Forward $600M: 40% tech/AI, 30% seeding, 30% M&A; supports 12-15% EPS growth, A- balance sheet.
